faqs.a: The four parts of a mortgage payment: Principal, Interest, property Tax, and homeowner's Insurance. Lenders quote PITI because it is the real monthly cost - this calculator adds PMI and HOA on top.
Put 20% down, or once you owe 80% or less of the home's value, ask your lender to drop PMI (they must drop it automatically at 78% for most conventional loans).
15-year: higher payment, much less total interest, faster equity. 30-year: lower payment, more flexibility, more interest. Many buyers take the 30-year and make extra payments - the best of both.
The 28/36 rule: keep housing under 28% of gross monthly income and all debts under 36%. Enter the resulting monthly budget here and work backwards to a price.
faqs.q: How much house can I afford?

faqs.a: Usually yes, via escrow: the lender collects 1/12 of the yearly tax each month and pays the bill for you. Same for homeowner's insurance.
faqs.q: Are property taxes included in my mortgage payment?

faqs.a: No. Everything is computed in your browser.

mortgage-calculator.formula:
Loan = price - down payment; r = rate/12/100; n = years x 12
P&I = loan x r / (1 - (1+r)^-n)
Tax = yearly tax / 12; Insurance = yearly / 12
PMI = loan x PMI rate / 12 (only if down < 20%)
Total = P&I + tax + insurance + PMI + HOA
howTo: Enter the home price and your down payment.
Enter the interest rate and loan term.
Add yearly property tax, yearly insurance, PMI rate, and monthly HOA.
Read the full monthly breakdown and the true total.
Try a bigger down payment to watch PMI disappear at 20%.
keyFacts: PITI = Principal + Interest + Tax + Insurance - the four parts of most mortgage payments.
PMI (private mortgage insurance) applies below 20% down and protects the lender, not you.
Property tax and insurance are usually escrowed - collected monthly, paid yearly by the lender.
A 15-year loan has higher payments but roughly half the lifetime interest of a 30-year.
The 28/36 rule: housing under 28% of gross income, all debt under 36%.
HOA dues are not part of the mortgage but are part of the monthly cost of the home.
